observation_summary: The application throws a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException when parsing a complex number string if the input string is too short to contain the expected imaginary character.
hypothesis: The code assumes that the input string has sufficient length to accommodate the imaginary character without verifying the bounds of the string relative to the current parse position and the length of the imaginary character.
prediction: The fix will introduce a conditional check to verify that the current index and the calculated end index are within the bounds of the source string before calling substring().
experiment_rationale: The provided fix diff explicitly adds boundary checks (startIndex >= source.length() || endIndex > source.length()) before the substring operation, confirming that the root cause was a missing validation of input bounds.
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic missing boundary check. The code attempts to extract a substring based on an expected length without verifying if the source string is long enough to support that operation. The fix adds the necessary conditional guards to prevent the StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, which is the definition of a Checking defect.
evidence_used: The stack trace shows a java.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at ComplexFormat.java:378.
The fix_diff_oracle shows the addition of (startIndex >= source.length()) || (endIndex > source.length()) before the substring call.
The bug report description states the method does not check if the source contains the imaginary character.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the logic is part of a method, the root cause is specifically the lack of a guard condition to validate input bounds, which is the hallmark of a Checking defect.
